answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. Consider a lantern as the anchor of the cost.
